'''Kenneth MacClure Baird''' (January 23, 1923 – April 18, 2022) was a Canadian physicist, [[metrologist]] and inventor, born of Canadian parents in China in 1923.

==Biography==
Baird received his [[Bachelor of Science]] in physics at the [[University of New Brunswick]], Canada in 1943, and joined the [[Canadian National Research Council]] (NRC) in Ottawa where he excelled at research in aerial reconnaissance and high speed photography.<ref name=one>"Physics at the National Research Council of Canada, 1929-1952" (1979). W.E.K. Middleton, p. 167</ref><ref name=two>US Patent 2687062, High Speed Camera, 1950. Kenneth M. Baird.</ref> In 1946 he created a camera which could snap 800,000 pictures a second.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Langan |first1=Fred |title=Scientist Kenneth Baird helped redefine the length of a metre |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-scientist-kenneth-baird-helped-redefine-the-length-of-a-metre/ |website=The Globe and Mail |access-date=24 September 2024 |date=18 May 2022}}</ref>

His success earned him full NRC financial support for graduate studies at Bristol University, England, where he acquired his Ph.D. in solid state physics in 1952.<ref name=three>{{cite web | url=http://www.osahistory.org/Home/Library/Biographies/Items/Kenneth-M--Baird/ | title=History &#124; Optica }}</ref> He is the younger brother to [[David McCurdy Baird|Dr. David Baird]].

Returning to the NRC, Baird headed the transition of Canada’s primary length standard/facilities of the International Metre from a prototype metal bar (the official international standard of length established in 1779)<ref name=nine>"Optic frequency/wavelength references," L. Hollberg et al. Journal of Physics B: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics, p. S472-S473 (2005)</ref> to a wavelength of light. His contribution to the development of isotope lamps, on perturbations to wavelength standards, and in interferometry<ref name=four>"A New Method in Optical Interferometry," Baird, K.M., JOSA, Vol. 44, Issue 1, p. 11-13 (1954)</ref><ref name=nineteen>"Excitation of Mercury-198 in a Liquid Nitrogen Cooled Hollow Cathode Lamp," Baird, K.M. and Hart, K.H., JOSA, Vol. 46, Issue 4 (1956)</ref><ref name=twenty>"Preliminary Measurements of Some Wavelengths of Krypton 86 and Mercury 198 Lines," Baird, K.M. and Smith, D.S., JOSA, Vol. 48, Issue 5, p. 300-301 (1958)</ref><ref name=twentyone>"Primary Standard of Length," Baird, K.M. and Smith, D.S., JOSA, Vol. 52, Issue 5, p.507-513 (1962)</ref><ref name=twentytwo>"Interference Comparators for Line Standards," K.M. Baird, Applied Optics, Vol. 2, Issue 5, p.471-479 (1963)</ref><ref name=twentythree>"Vacuum Wavelengths of Kr86, Hg198 and Cd114", Baird, K.M.; Smith, D.S., and Hart, K.H., JOSA, Vol. 53, Issue 6, p.717-720 (1963)</ref><ref name=twentyfour>"The International Length Standard," Baird, K.M. and Howlett, L.E., Applied Optics, Vol. 2, Issue 5, p. 455-463 (1963)</ref> (including the development of the world’s first interference comparator for metre bar calibration in terms of standard wavelengths) placed Canada among the main contributors to the redefinition of the International Metre in 1960.<ref name=nine /><ref name=five>"Adoption of the Wavelength Definition of the Meter," December 1960, National Bureau of Standards Technical News Bulletin</ref><ref name=six>"Definition of the Metre", The International Bureau of Weights & Measures, The International System of Units, 11th CGPM, 1960, p.148</ref>

Baird also maintained Canada’s primary standard of mass as well as length, and standards for quantities derived from them, such as density, pressure, vacuum and certain engineering standards. For much of this work Baird engaged the industrial community, producing results such as the first commercially produced internal reflector laser,<ref name=three /> manufactured by E. Leitz Company. In 1973, Baird and his colleagues invented an important interference device<ref name=seven>"Optical Interference Coatings for Inhibiting of Counterfeiting," J.A. Dobrowolski, K.M. Baird, P.D. Carman and A. Waldorf, International Journal of Optics, Vol. 20, Issue 12 (1973)</ref><ref name=eight>US Patent 3858977, Optical Interference Authenticating Means, 1973. Kenneth M. Baird, Jerzy A. Dobrowolski, Allan J. Waldorf, Philip D. Carman.</ref> designed for the security of valuable documents, subsequently used on Canadian monetary bills thus establishing a new standard for currency anti-counterfeiting.

Baird and his colleagues worked to improve the accuracy of measurements of the speed of light, which ultimately provided the solid foundation for redefining the International Metre in 1982<ref name=ten>"News from the Bureau Inter’l des Poids et Mesures," J. Terrien, International Bureau of Weights and Measurements, F.92310, p.76 (1973)</ref><ref name=twelve>"Optic frequency/wavelength references," L. Hollberg et al. Journal of Physics B: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics, p. S474-S475 (2005)</ref><ref name=eighteen>"Definition of the Metre," The International Bureau of Weights & Measurements, The International System of Units, 17th CPGM, 1983, p.160</ref> and "their skilled pioneering work in laser frequency stabilization and measurement" which resulted in the following achievements:

* The development of the Iodine-stabilized helium neon laser, and one of the first demonstrations of saturated [[absorption spectroscopy]] and widely used realization of the primary standard of length and wavelengths.<ref name=eleven>"Characteristics of a Simple Single-Mode He-Ne Laser," K.M. Baird, D.S. Smith, G.R. Hanes and S. Tsunekane, Applied Optics, Vol. 4, Issue 5, p. 569-571 (1965)</ref><ref name=twentyfive>"I2 Controlled He-N e laser at 633nm: preliminary wavelength," Hanes, G.R. and Baird, K.M., Metrologia (1969), 5(1), p.32-33</ref><ref name=twentysix>US Patent 3528028, Gaseous Laser of Improved Construction, 1970. Kenneth M. Baird.</ref><ref name=twentyseven>"CO2 wavelengths and the velocity of light," 1972, Baird, K.M., Riccius, H.D., Siemsen, K.J., NRC Institute for National Measurement Standards.</ref><ref name=twentyeight>"Optic frequency/wavelength references," L. Hollberg et al. Journal of Physics B: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics, p. S471 (2005)</ref><ref name=seventeen>"Fundamental Spectroscopic Data," Transactions of the International Astronomical Union, Vol. XVIIA, Reports 1979, p. 155-157, K.G. Kessler.</ref>
* The confirmation of the most recent new values for the speed of light, 100 times more accurate than previous measurements (The 7th International Conference on Quantum Electronics, Montreal, 1972).<ref name=fifteen>"Confirmation of the Currently Accepted Value 299 792 458 Metres per Second for the Speed of Light", K.M. Baird, D.S. Smith and B.G. Whitford, Optics Communications, September 24, 1979</ref>
* The development of the technique of transition–difference generated frequencies in spectroscopic wavelength and frequency measurements.<ref name=nine /><ref name=ten /><ref name=twelve /><ref name=eleven /><ref name=fourteen>"Extension of absolute-frequency measurements to the visible: frequencies of ten hyperfine components of iodine," K.M. Baird, K.M. Evenson, G.R. Hanes, D.A. Jennings and F.R. Petersen. Optics Letters, Vol. 4, Issue 9, p.263-264 (1979)</ref>
* The first measurement of the frequency of visible light,<ref name=eleven /> in collaboration with the US National Bureau of Standards.<ref name=three /><ref name=fifteen /><ref name=sixteen>"Optical Frequency Measurement at NRC and Progress Towards Frequency Measurement of Visible Light," K.M. Baird, D.S. Smith and B.G. Whitford. Optics Communications, September 24, 1979.</ref>

Baird held five patents, and has over fifty scientific and technical papers published in the fields of high-speed and aerial photography, interferometry, lasers and metrology, establishing him as one of North America’s foremost metrologists, and giving Canada a great reputation in this field.<ref name=thirteen>"Physics at the National Research Council of Canada, 1929-1952" (1979). W.E.K. Middleton, p.163</ref> As an invited guest, he has spoken at the Gaithersburg Conferences on Precision Measurements and Fundamental Constants in 1970 and 1981; the Fifth International Conference on Laser Spectroscopy at the U.R.S.I. Commission (Washington, DC); the Third Symposium on Frequency Standards and Metrology (France); the Royal Society Meeting on New Techniques in Optical and Infrared Spectroscopy (London); and the NATO Advanced Study Institute on [[Quantum metrology|Quantum Metrology]] (Italy).<ref name=three />

Baird was an active member of the Optical Society of America, of which he was a fellow and member/chairman of several technical groups and policy committees. He was a member of its board of directors, vice president and president in 1983. In 1989, he was awarded its C.E.K. Mees Medal "in recognition of his contributions to standards research and optical metrology and of his service to the International Commission for Optics and the Optical Society of America."<ref name=three />

Baird was also a member of the [[Canadian Association of Physicists]] and chairman of its Optical Physics Division; president of the International Commission of Optics (IUPAP – a Division of UNESCO); a member of the [[International Astronomical Union]] (IAU) and chairman of its working group on wavelength standards; a member of the International Advisory Committee for the Definition of the Metre and steering committee chairman for the redefinition of the metre in 1982, as well as serving on advisory boards for several optical journals.<ref name=three />

After retirement from the NRC in 1982, he was a visiting fellow at the Joint Institute of Laboratory Astrophysics (University of Colorado) and in 1983 a visiting scientist at the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organization in Sydney, Australia.<ref name=three />

While studying at the [[University of Bristol]], England, Baird met his Swiss wife of 60 years, Erna Jaggi Baird, who died June 6, 2011, of a rare autoimmune disease:<ref>[https://www.uhnfdn.ca/ebmg/ "Erna Baird Memorial Grant"].</ref>

In 2015, Baird was the eldest recipient to be named a Member of the [[Order of Canada]].<ref>[http://www.ottawasun.com/2015/11/18/scientist-hopes-for-renewed-optimismoneplan "Scientist Hopes for Renewed Optimism"]. ''[[Ottawa Sun]]'', November 18, 2015.</ref>

Baird died in Ottawa on April 18, 2022, at the age of 99.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kenneth MacClure Baird |url=https://www.legacy.com/ca/obituaries/theglobeandmail/name/kenneth-baird-obituary?pid=201905797 |website=Legacy |access-date=3 May 2022}}</ref>
